finding: src/anomaly/_attempt_workspace.py:40 Promotion cleanup deletes the attempt workspace before clearing the interrupted-promotion marker, so a real final-cleanup interruption can produce a manual-repair block that points to a workspace that no longer exists.
rationale: The public workflow reaches this ordering with no guard: promotion writes the marker, commits artifacts and state, removes the workspace, and only then unlinks the marker; an interruption between the two cleanup calls leaves a marker that startup converts into a blocked result instructing the journalist to inspect the already-deleted workspace, violating the retained-workspace acceptance criterion even though live artifacts fail safe.

evidence.output: Lines 35-41: marker_path is written at line 37; _apply and write_state complete at lines 38-39; discard_workspace(workspace) runs at line 40 before marker_path.unlink() at line 41. Lines 44-69: recover_interrupted_promotion treats any remaining marker as interrupted, marks the case blocked, and sets blocked_reason to 'inspect retained workspace {attempt_path}/workspace' without checking that the workspace exists.
